goals: Mechanistic: characterize how soil texture and forcing period control ELM simulated sub-surface recharge across the Naches domain
Validation/falsification: test whether 500 mm/yr is a defensible domain value or whether recharge is spatially variable — NOT to confirm a fixed number
key_processes: water partitioning (ET vs runoff vs drainage)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves water partitioning and sub-surface drainage/recharge, the quantity in question; spatial sampling spans domain soil heterogeneity.

answerable: Soil-texture control on simulated recharge across the domain
Whether the simulated recharge distribution supports or refutes a uniform 500 mm/yr value
Indirect WTD validation against USGS wells / Fan 2013 prior

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation/confirmation of recharge magnitude (the 500 mm/yr claim)
not_answerable.why: observations_missing lists recharge measurements — no in-domain recharge data exists to confirm any value

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation/snow/orographic-precipitation control on recharge across 352-1977 m
not_answerable.why: framework uses uniform forcing with no elevation downscaling; elevation-stratified columns would reflect soil, not climate gradient

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by dominant soil class, with temporal sampling over the forcing record
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 dominant soil classes span the primary resolvable recharge control; light replication (2 per class) captures within-class variation from secondary soil/depth differences sampled by the expander. Forcing spread is handled temporally over 1980-2018 rather than by adding columns.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute across the domain to capture the dominant soil classes; oversample valley-bottom/lower-elevation soils where the water table is shallow and recharge-to-WTD linkage is strongest and where USGS wells are more likely to co-locate for validation.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per soil class to expose within-class heterogeneity; not intended as statistical replication.

sampling_plan.reason: high-permeability soils bound the high-recharge / low-ET end of the partitioning response
intermediate texture represents the domain-typical recharge behavior for comparison to the 500 mm/yr claim
low-permeability soils bound the low-recharge / high-runoff end and test spatial uniformity of recharge

validation_design.comparison: co-located where wells fall near sampled columns; aggregated/analog against Fan 2013 prior elsewhere — indirect constraint on the drainage/recharge regime, not a direct recharge check
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in-domain

validation_design.comparison: cannot be validated in-domain; report simulated distribution and compare against the literature 500 mm/yr claim as a hypothesis test, not a confirmation
validation_design.metric: distribution summary (median, spread) vs claimed 500 mm/yr

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline uniform forcing (1980-2018), native soil per column

requires_capabilities.why: no recharge measurements exist to confirm or refute the 500 mm/yr claim directly
uniform forcing cannot represent the orographic precip / snow gradient that dominates recharge over 352-1977 m
expander must assign soil class per column from real rasters

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well ingest + HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: to locate in-domain wells for WTD validation
recharge/WTD equilibration required before interpreting fluxes

assumptions: The user's premise that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to test, not a target to reproduce; the design is built to falsify it if the model disagrees.
Dominant soil classes reduce to ~3 texture groups; actual classes assigned downstream from soil rasters.
Uniform baseline forcing over 1980-2018; interannual variability sampled temporally.
WTD is used only as an indirect constraint on the drainage regime, not as a recharge measurement.
open_questions: What is the source/definition of the published 500 mm/yr value (annual mean? specific soil/elevation? method)? Needed to make a fair comparison.
How many USGS wells fall within the HUC and what is their depth/period of record?
Should recharge be reported as QDRAI, QRECHARGE, or net drainage below the root zone?
